correctness.rationale: A D_r(D_sX) vertex is exactly an unordered partition of one rs-element face U of X into r disjoint s-blocks. This gives c=(rs)!/(r!(s!)^r) equally many labels per U. Two or more labels form a simplex iff underlying rs-sets are distinct, disjoint and have union in X; this proves a natural isomorphism to uniform vertex inflation of K=D_rsX, without dimension or connectedness restrictions. Links satisfy lk_K(F)=D_rs(lk_X(U_F)). For connected K the Björner–Wachs–Welker Theorem 6.2 vertex-inflation wedge splitting directly supplies the integral formula with (c−1)^|F| copies of Σ^|F| of those links; disconnected components are handled separately, and the empty-facet link has S^{|F|−1} convention. X=Δ⁵ gives 10 vs 15 isolated vertices for (r,s)=(2,3) and (3,2), and X=Δ⁸ gives 378 vertices, 2835 edges, beta1 2458. The proof checks all face levels, not only 1-skeleton; inspected verifier independently constructs direct and partition-labelled small cases. This is a valid consequence of the earlier splitting, which is credited, not newly proved.
